//counts: Measured 2026-10-10 after routing the scribe into SOAP: 2185/1443/735/7 with NO database, and 2185/2180/0/5 against a local PostgreSQL 17.10. +3 over the consent-gate figures, all three database-free, so the SKIPPED ceiling did not move. Client 409. THE RULE DID NOT CHANGE; IT MOVED TO THE RIGHT PLACE. The scribe used to draft the Subjective and nothing else, on the rule that a model drafting an assessment is a model making a clinical decision. That rule stands. What was wrong is WHERE it sat: when a pharmacist says out loud "chest is clear, looks viral, honey and fluids, come back in five days", the assessment and the plan were MADE BY A PERSON, and writing them into the right boxes is transcription. Refusing was not safety, it was making a pharmacist retype a decision they had already spoken. So the line moved from WHICH SECTION to WHOSE WORDS: the patient’s voice drafts Subjective and nothing else, the pharmacist’s drafts Objective, Assessment and Plan, and a voice that said nothing drafts nothing. The structured records (problems, interventions, referral, prescription, care-program, summary) stay forbidden, and now for a sharper reason: they are not prose but records with their own validation and their own audit trail. ONE model call with both halves labelled, because the owner asked for swift and this deployment’s model reasons for seconds - but the labelling is a HINT and each section is then validated against the words of the person who owns it, so a model that files the pharmacist’s advice as the patient’s report is caught rather than trusted. A NEW REFUSAL, hardenedACertainty: an assessment that drops a hedge the pharmacist used. "I think it MIGHT be viral" filed as "Viral upper respiratory infection" has turned a working impression into a diagnosis and the next reader cannot tell. Asked only of the Assessment, because that is the section where certainty IS the clinical content. WITHINTRANSCRIPT BECAME A RATIO, and this is a LOOSENING named as one. The first live run refused the Subjective as longer_than_transcript at 462 characters from 444 of speech - FOUR PER CENT over, on the normal case, for the most important section. Measured: subjective 1.04, objective 0.21, assessment 0.24, plan 0.44, because the Subjective covers ALL of a patient’s speech while the others cover part of the pharmacist’s. Capped at 1.5 now. It still catches a model answering a short recording with paragraphs; it never caught a fabricated symptom that fits inside the budget, at any threshold, because that is SHORTER - which needs entity-level grounding and has its own task. Six mutations run against the new safety logic and all six turned the right test red. TWO EXISTING INVARIANTS WERE AMENDED WITH THE PRODUCT, NOT RELAXED. scribeContract’s pinned SCRIBABLE === [subjective]; it now pins the stronger claim that every section is drafted from the voice that owns it AND that a forbidden section has no owning voice at all. consultationLayout’s microphone invariant pinned an early return the mode machine replaced; it now pins REACHABILITY - the microphone is opened in exactly one place, that place renders only under mode ready, and ready is reachable only via a consented note or the server’s own acceptance of consent. Measured again 2026-10-11 after adding counter patient creation: 2192/1450/735/7 with NO database and 2192/2187/0/5 with one. +7, all database-free, so the skipped ceiling did not move. The feature is an INSERT NOBODY WROTE: the route calls customerIdentity.resolveCustomer, the existing upsert that is atomic by constraint, rather than inserting into customers itself - because identity_key is unique per pharmacy and a hand-written INSERT would have worked today and produced a DUPLICATE the first time that person texted. Proven against a real database: 0803 999 1122 typed at the counter creates (201); +2348039991122 returns the SAME id with created:false (200); and the same number arriving over WhatsApp resolves to that same row, leaving ONE row for the identity, with the pharmacist's full_name surviving while display_name becomes what WhatsApp calls them (the 0020 split). A PHONE NUMBER IS REQUIRED and that is a schema fact: wa_jid is NOT NULL (0016) and identity_key is NOT NULL (0019). A walk-in with NO phone is therefore not supported, and supporting one means making wa_jid nullable, which is a change to the live identity path and belongs in its own commit. wa_jid is synthesised as <number>@s.whatsapp.net and overwritten with the real one on first message; nothing can send to it meanwhile because messageInput's outreach gate refuses a patient who has not written first. 8 mutations run and the EIGHTH WAS MISSED, which taught something: deleting the required-phone check still refuses an empty box, falling through to the parser and saying "that does not look like a phone number" - safe, and wrong for the person, because an empty field is not a malformed one. The test now asserts the MESSAGE and the mutation then failed.

//lastChange: Workflows: what the assistant does on a pharmacy’s behalf, made visible (AGENTIC_PLAN.md phase 1, 2026-10-12). THE ENGINE WAS RUNNING HEADLESS. A governed clinical engine has been in this product for months - versioned protocols, a red-flag evaluator, a safety gate, a router whose header says routing is "only ever a NARROWING" - and THREE protocols route real patients’ WhatsApp messages. There was no protocols endpoint and no protocol screen, so a pharmacy could not see which protocols run in its name, what they ask, which version, or whether one is switched on. THE DRIFT THAT PROVES THE POINT, and it is why this is worth more than a screen: client/src/modules.js advertised "Malaria assessment" with status: active, while nigeriaMalariaAssessmentV1.js says in capitals on its second line "DRAFT. NOT ACTIVE. NOT PATIENT-FACING." The same file’s own comment states the principle it was breaking - unbuilt services are "deliberately ABSENT... listing them would promise a service a pharmacy cannot offer". Nobody lied; there was no screen, no endpoint and no test that could notice. server/tests/protocols.test.js now pins it. THREE FACTS, NEVER COLLAPSED: a file existing, the router knowing about it (wiredUp), and this pharmacy having it active (live, per tenant from the database). Only the last means a patient will be asked these questions tonight. A FOURTH state exists because isProtocolLive fails CLOSED - "an unreadable configuration is not permission to start a clinical workflow" - which is right for routing and wrong for a screen: reporting a failed read as "switched off" tells a pharmacy something nobody checked. READ-ONLY, AND THE REFERENCE’S "Create workflow" BUTTON IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. clinicalProtocolService.js says interpreting a protocol is "a later stage’s job, under clinical governance this module has no part in", and a web form that writes clinical question sets is that change wearing a UI. The screen also drops the reference’s Discover and Pinned tabs: we have no community library and no pinning, and shipping empty tabs would be the screen promising what the product does not have - the exact defect it exists to surface. clinicalRouter gained ONE read-only export, listRoutableProtocols(), returning the same memoised candidate list route already builds, so the screen cannot show a protocol the router would not consider nor miss one it would. No routing behaviour changed. The questions are shown VERBATIM - 12 for fever v2 - because that is the part a patient actually experiences, with the clinical source cited (Nigeria Standard Treatment Guidelines 2022 p242). Two versions ship together and differ visibly: fever v1 asks 7 questions with ZERO red flags, v2 asks 12 with eight. 7 server tests, ALL DATABASE-FREE so they run on the committed default, and 13 client tests. 12 mutations run. TWO OF MY OWN MISTAKES, both caught before commit: a test asserting the screen has no "Create workflow" button FAILED because that phrase appeared in a comment I had just written explaining why there is none - the comment was reworded and the test left alone, which is GOLDEN-006’s precedent applied to me; and mutation 10 was MISSED because the test matched the filename anywhere in the route file, including the header comment that names the malaria protocol while explaining the drift - it now parses the SHIPPED list itself, and the mutation then failed. modules.test.js was AMENDED with the product, as it was when Consultations joined Clinics: the Clinics sidebar literal gains "workflows". The rule it pins - no clinical service without a screen reaches the sidebar - is unchanged and still passes. Client 396 -> 409. Server 2192 -> 2199 (+7 pass, same 5 known failures, 0 skipped with a test database).
